title: Use of High-Throughput Automated Microbioreactor System for Production of Model IgG1 in CHO Cells
protocol: Rapidly thaw stock vial(s) of CHO cells by immersing in a 37 °C water bath until only a small sliver of ice remains.
Decontaminate the outside of the vial using 70% ethanol solution and a lint-free tissue.
Transfer to a biosafety cabinet.
Re-suspend cells by gently pipetting up and down.
Transfer 1 mL to a sterile 125 mL vented shake flask containing 29 mL pre-warmed media supplemented with 8 mM L-glutamine and 1x Penicillin/Streptomycin.
Place shake flask(s) in an incubator maintained at 37 °C and 8% CO2.
Use an orbital shaker to agitate cells at a speed of 130 rpm.
Monitor the viable cell density (VCD) every day using an automated cell counting device or manually with a hemocytometer and trypan blue.
Subculture cells 72 hours after inoculation in fresh media by diluting such that the final volume is 100 mL in a 125 mL spinner flask.
Pre-warm the media to 37 °C every time it must be added to cells.
Incubate spinner cultures at the same conditions used for shake flask cultures at a speed of 70 rpm.
Add fresh, pre-warmed media to spinner-flask(s) on day three (one day prior to inoculum preparations) to maintain ≥ 90% viability.
Do not exceed 125 mL total volume.
Connect to Cell counter remote connection before opening the software.
Click on the remote desktop icon and click on "Connect."
Open the cell counter software.
Install a new reagent pack.
Empty the trypan blue waste.
Prime the system.
Minimize the remote connection.
Open the micro bioreactor software using an existing experiment as a template to create a new experiment.
Name and save the experiment.
Ensure that the automated cell counter is connected under the status tab in the software.
Check the status on the cell counter software.
Define plates used during the run in the mimic section of the software.
Name each plate used.
Designate each plate to a deck on the microbioreactor culture station.
Use a 24-well plate for media charging and place it on the designated deck of the culture station.
Place 1 mL pipet tip boxes in the sections as indicated.
Place 4 mL pipet tip boxes in the sections as indicated.
Place a 24-well inoculation plate on the respective deck of the culture station.
Place the single-well 1X phosphate buffered saline (PBS) plate on deck 1.
Place the single-well 1 M NaOH plate on deck 2.
Place the 24-well antifoam plate on deck 7.
Unpack the culture vessels equipped with sparger inside the safety cabinet hood.
Place twelve sterile culture vessels per culture station.
Place autoclaved clamp plates on top of the vessels.
Check that the holes in inserts provided for stirrers all face the same direction.
Place the stir plates on top of the clamp plates, ensuring each pin is securely inserted.
Secure the clamp plates with the screws and knobs provided.
Tighten the knobs till they are hand tight.
Tighten left and right knobs alternatively for even placement of the clamp plate.
Check that the clamp is flush against the surface.
Ensure screws at the end of the clamp plate are evenly tightened.
Inspect O-rings to confirm complete sealing of plates.
Run the Automated Micro Bioreactor Software.
Use "Process Steps" tab to edit or create new steps.
Click "Insert Step" button under the process steps tab to create new steps.
Double click on an existing step to edit that step.
Initialize and check for presence of appropriate vessels.
Scan the barcode provided with the culture vessels.
Commence the designed program after checking DO control, gassing and other connections.
Load pipet tips, both 1 mL and 4 mL tips, as programmed.
Place the media plate, 1X PBS, 1 M NaOH, antifoam plate, media charging plate and inoculation plate in the designated decks.
Begin temperature control and set temperature to 37 °C.
Switch on stirring at 1000 rpm and the DO/pH monitor.
Execute the media charging program.
Dispense media from the media plate to the culture vessels as mapped in the program.
Use two wells from a 24-well plate to fill one culture vessel to capacity (13 mL).
Add 7-8 mL of media to each well to prevent air drawing during mixing by the liquid handler prior to charging.
Charge the culture vessel with mixed media.
Add 35 μL of Ex-Cell antifoam to the culture vessel from an antifoam plate.
Allow 30 minutes for the culture medium to be well mixed and optical DO/pH sensors to hydrate.
Monitor foaming visually every day, adding intermittent volumes of antifoam when detected.
Switch on DO/pH control once equilibration is achieved.
Turn on background base additions to attain a pH set point of 7.1 for all culture vessels.
Allow overnight DO and pH stabilization.
Execute the paused pH step the next day (marked as day 1) to determine pH correction offset.
Place the sample tube holder plates on designated decks.
Load micro centrifuge tubes with caps open and tucked beside them.
Remove a sample immediately after liquid handler dispenses 600 µL of cell culture fluid into the tube.
Measure pH on a nutrient bioanalyzer that has been properly calibrated.
Enter external, FLEX-derived pH values in the software.
Manually average the offsets obtained for the sample vessels.
Enter the number under the user pH offset column under the tab "Vessel Data".
Apply the averaged offset to all the vessels.
Allow the pH to equilibrate for at least 2-3 hours.
Transfer entire contents of spinner-flask(s) into a sterile, 250 mL conical centrifuge tube after measuring VCD.
Pellet cells by centrifuging for 10 min at 140 x g at room temperature.
Decant the old media.
Re-suspend in enough fresh media such that the final density should be 1x106 cells/mL.
Add suspended cells into a designated well of a sterile lidded 24-well plate.
Add 3 mL of inoculum to each well.
Remove 2 mL of inoculum for each culture vessel.
Spray the outside of the lidded inoculum plate with 70% alcohol before placing it inside the hood.
Place the inoculum plate on the designated deck inside the hood.
Let the culture vessels equilibrate for at least an hour after inoculation.
Execute the 5X cell count step in the program after an hour.
Add 480 µL of 1X PBS to the cell counter cup.
Add 120 µL of cell culture fluid from each vessel to the cell counter cup.
Read the cell count using the automated cell counter.
Repeat the cell counting process for all vessels.
Record daily cell count data, including viable cell density and viability.
Clean the cell counter cup at least twice during the duration of the run with 70% IPA.
Repeat the "Paused pH" step on day 2 using culture vessels different from those sampled initially.
Sample more vessel population for paused pH to provide better offset for pH correction.
Do not sample the same vessels used for paused pH from the previous day.
Take samples for nutrient analysis from Day 2 of culture until experiment end.
Place sample tube holder plates on designated decks.
Load micro centrifuge tubes with caps open and tucked beside them.
Dispense cell culture fluid into the tube as mapped in the program by liquid handler.
Dilute samples taken initially (days 2 - 4) with 300 μL of 1X PBS for analysis.
Place samples in analyzer tray to perform nutrient analysis.
Freeze any samples not to be analyzed on the same day.
Turn off the temperature control and agitation in sequence.
Stop the DO/pH control and background base additions.
Stop all other controls.
Stop the system monitor.
Unscrew the clamp and stir plates, then remove culture vessels.
Clean the inside of the culture station with a lint-free wipe.
Place drying plates on the culture station and screw them in.
Execute the 2-hour drying cycle for cooled systems only.
Clean the clamp plates using ultrapure water followed by 70% IPA to remove condensed liquid.
Flush with air to remove any residual liquid.
Click "Stop" in the bioreactor software once the drying cycle has finished.
Transfer cell culture fluid from reactor vessels.
Pellet cells at 1,962 x g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Decant and discard the supernatant.
Filter the decanted cell culture fluid using a 0.22 µm PVDF filter.
Aliquot 1 mL of sterile cell culture fluid into 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes for titer analysis.
Store the aliquots at -20 °C.
Purify the rest of the harvested cell culture fluid using fast protein liquid chromatography system.
Turn on the system and allow the lamp to warm up for at least 1 hour.
Remove samples from freezer to thaw and equilibrate to room temperature.
Set the plate temperature to 26 °C in the system software.
Pre-soak the number of Protein A tips to be used in sample matrix for at least 30 minutes.
Incubate the sample plate on the sample stage for ≥ 10 minutes to pre-equilibrate samples to the chosen assay temperature.
Build a protein standard curve using an antibody concentrated to 10 mg/mL and serially dilute in the sample matrix.
Design the sample plate according to the specified layout.
Include up to 80 samples on each plate, including unknown culture samples, standards, and controls.
Use a single protein A tip to measure up to 10 samples across the plate (columns 1-10).
Regenerate the tip between each sample measurement.
Designate the entire first row of the plate as negative control and reference.
Utilize rows B and C for two positive controls: one at the lower limit and another at the upper limit of the linear response.
Ensure each tip measures negative and positive controls before analyzing samples.
Use remaining wells for unknown samples.
Place sample matrix in any well where there is a gap to prevent drying of the tip.
Do not reuse tips between different plates; use a new, non-regenerated set for every plate.
Gently mix samples either by inversion or pipetting.
Pulse spin samples to collect at the bottom of the tube.
Dilute concentrated samples in sample matrix as needed.
Prepare 96-well sample plates close to assay time.
Remove air bubbles from wells with a clean pipette tip or centrifugation.
Load plate into the BLI system.
Run assay using the "High Sensitivity Assay with Regeneration" setting.
Analyze data using HT Data Analysis software.
Subtract reference and calculate unknown concentrations using standard curve and initial slope function.
